Article Title: Wall Street's AI jitters return as stocks tumble, S&P500 logs longest losing streak in 2.5 years
Article Text:
Wall Street takes another hit

Anthropic's strong debut fails to lift mood

AI stocks give up early gains as selling returns

AI bubble: Why investors are worried

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Asian markets mixed, European stocks end lower

Wall Street took another hit on Thursday as the AI party appeared to be losing its fizz. US stocks tumbled again as investors continued to dump AI-linked shares, questioning whether the technology's spectacular rally had finally run out of steam.Even Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut, which saw its shares soar well above the expected price, failed to lift the mood, as worries over sky-high valuations, expensive borrowing and whether massive AI investments will pay off kept investors on edge.The S&P500 fell 2%, marking its sixth straight day of losses. This is its longest losing streak in two and a half years. The index is now 8.2% below the record high it touched last month.The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points, or 2.3%. The sell-off was broad-based, with more than 90% of the stocks in the S&P500 ending the day lower.The market initially showed signs of recovery after Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, made its stock market debut on Thursday.The company priced its shares at $83 each, higher than its earlier expected range of $70 to $78.Soon after trading began on the Nasdaq shortly before noon, the shares climbed above $115.The strong debut briefly lifted the S&P500 by as much as 1.3%. However, the gains did not last. Anthropic shares eventually closed at $97.17, up 17.1% from their IPO price.The strong demand for the shares showed that investors were still interested in AI companies, despite the recent fall in their stock prices. However, the positive response to Anthropic's listing was not enough to stop the wider market decline.Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, described the current market conditions as “a very turbulent, white-knuckle period.”Several major AI-linked stocks started Thursday's session with gains but later slipped into losses.Micron Technology, which has benefited from rising demand for computer memory because of the AI boom, initially gained 7.8%. However, it reversed course and ended the day 2.1% lower.CoreWeave, which buys AI chips and rents access to them to customers through the cloud, also saw its shares swing sharply. After rising 10.5% in the morning, the stock ended the session down 6.1%.Nvidia shares followed a similar pattern. The stock erased its early gain of 4.7% and closed 3.3% lower as concerns about the AI industry continued to weigh on investors.The recent fall in AI stocks comes amid growing concerns about whether their high prices can be justified.One of the biggest worries is that shares of AI companies may have become too expensive after their sharp rise. Investors are also questioning whether AI will generate enough profits and improve productivity enough to justify the huge amounts companies are spending on data centres.High interest rates have added to these concerns. With borrowing becoming more expensive, investors fear that companies may find it harder to raise the money needed to expand their AI businesses.Political developments have also added to the uncertainty. Sweeping victories for Democrats in the US midterm elections this month have raised concerns that AI companies could face more regulations.Another development adding to the concerns was the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang was one of the biggest supporters of the AI industry and helped build investor interest in the technology. He also used some of Nvidia's huge profits to support the industry's growth.In the bond market, US treasury yields declined as investors moved towards investments considered safer amid the fall in stock prices.The yield on the 10-year US Treasury slipped to 5.04% from 5.07% on Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, so when bond prices rise, their yields fall.Elsewhere, stock markets remained mixed.Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.7%, helped by a 4.6% gain in SoftBank Group. The company was an early investor in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and a competitor to Anthropic.South Korea's Kospi also gained 1.4%, supported by a rise in stocks linked to the AI boom.However, stocks were weaker in other parts of Asia and Europe. Germany's DAX fell 1.1%.At the end of Thursday's trading session, the S&P 500 dropped 147.80 points to 7,175.83. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,101.11 points to close at 49,097.06, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points to 23,879.20.
Article Summary: The S&P500 fell 2%, marking its sixth straight day of losses. This is its longest losing streak in two and a half years. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%. Even Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut failed to lift the mood.

Article Title: EPFO approves SWP for retirees to withdraw PF savings in regular instalments; relaxes minimum balance to 10%
Article Text:
According to the EPFO, the initiative will strengthen financial security after retirement.

What is EPFO’s SWP for your PF account?

Minimum balance requirements and more

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a big move that will benefit lakhs of provident fund subscribers, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ). The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today. Under the proposed facility, members will be able to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in instalments over a period of time instead of taking out the entire amount at once.Under the proposed facility, retirees will be able to choose the frequency of their withdrawals, with options including monthly, quarterly and half-yearly payments.This will give members a structured source of regular income while allowing the balance of their provident fund corpus to remain invested and continue generating returns, the government release said.Participation in the scheme will be entirely voluntary, and members will not be required to opt for periodic withdrawals.The facility may also be extended to eligible family members and beneficiaries, offering households greater flexibility and financial protection.The objectives include ensuring a steady income after retirement, lowering reinvestment risks, supporting the sustainability of the fund and widening social security coverage to gig and platform workers.The SWP will allow retirees to receive predictable payments from their accumulated savings without giving up ownership of the remaining corpus.In the initial phase, around 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years, each with provident fund savings of over Rs 5 lakh, are expected to be the main beneficiaries of the proposed arrangement.If a member dies while receiving SWP payments, the nominee or dependent will be able to either withdraw the outstanding balance or continue receiving instalments.To offer greater flexibility and advance the objective of universal social security, the proposal also envisages UAN-linked facilities for direct voluntary deposits and small contributions from third parties, including customer tips.These payments will be possible independently of conventional employer payroll systems.The required amendments to the EPF Scheme will be notified after approval from the Ministry. A corresponding amendment to the Income Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance.The board approved revisions to the minimum balance and waiting period provisions governing withdrawals.Under the earlier arrangement, members were required to retain 25% of their contributions in their accounts as a minimum balance at all times.The prescribed minimum has now been lowered from 25% to 10%.The waiting period for withdrawal has also been cut from 12 months to two months.These changes are intended to give EPF members greater access to their money while continuing to protect their long-term social security interests.The board also cleared amendments to the EDLI Scheme, 2026, to help resolve pending legacy exemption cases and give eligible establishments six months to renew exemptions that have expired.
Article Summary: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ). The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today.

Article Title: No invite for China at Anthropic IPO: After SpaceX, Claude parent too shuts Chinese investors out
Article Text:
Anthropic IPO

Why keep Chinese investors at arm's length?

Trump and Xi may be talking, but technology remains a sticking point

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!Earlier billionaire Elon Musk's AI and aerospace giant SpaceX barred investors from Hong Kong and mainland China from buying its shares. Now, Anthropic followed a similar route. While the IPO was open only to investors from selected countries, the repeated exclusion of Chinese investors by major US technology companies raises questions.The artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot reportedly turned away investment from Chinese and Hong Kong firms ahead of its public listing, in what went on to record as the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history.Three people familiar with the decision said Anthropic had excluded investors from the two regions, New York Times reported.The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. As Washington and Beijing compete for supremacy in AI, technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in their already strained relationship.The exclusion comes against the backdrop of a growing technology rivalry between the US and China.The Trump administration has been taking steps to restrict China's access to advanced AI technology, while both countries are drawing red lines around their homegrown technologies.Anthropic's decision appears in line with a wider trend among major American technology companies. SpaceX and its bankers had taken a similar step ahead of the company's blockbuster IPO in July, shutting Chinese investors out of the offering.OpenAI, another leading AI company, is also expected to bar Chinese investors from its eventual public listing. It has already prevented investors from China from participating in its private fund-raising rounds.There is another common thread connecting all three companies: Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI have all counted the US government among their clients.The decision also comes at an interesting moment in US-China relations. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on Thursday at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, China, with both leaders looking to bring some stability and goodwill into an increasingly rocky economic relationship.During the meeting, Xi called on members to build an "open ecosystem" for technology. Yet, while the two leaders are attempting to improve ties, their governments continue to build barriers around trade, technology and capital.The latest developments around AI chips underline just how difficult that balancing act is. Hours before Trump arrived in Asia for meetings with regional leaders, his administration moved to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.Beijing was quick to warn that it could respond with countermeasures if Washington continued with the restrictions."If the US persists, China will take countermeasures," China warned.A spokesman for China's Ministry of Commerce also expressed strong opposition to the latest US measures on Thursday."China is deeply concerned about — and firmly opposes — a series of recent economic and trade restrictive measures taken by the US against China," the spokesman told NYT.The latest restrictions on artificial intelligence are adding to a series of escalating moves by both countries. China experts have warned that the new AI rule could make it harder for Trump and Xi to reach any meaningful agreement to ease tensions.
Article Summary: Anthropic turned away Chinese and Hong Kong investors ahead of its IPO. Elon Musk's SpaceX also barred Chinese investors from its IPO in July. The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. Technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in US-China relations.

Article Title: $20 billion each! Meet the Anthropic co-founders who struck gold with IPO

Anthropic makes a stellar debut at Wall Street

Anthropic co-founders: Who holds how much?

Employees: 5,100 millionaires, 600 centi-millionaires

Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut has created a massive wealth windfall for its founders, employees and early investors, with individual stakes running into billions of dollars. While co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei has an estimated shareholding worth $20.07 billion, other co-founders are not far behind, with each holding equity valued at nearly $20 billion.The Claude chatbot maker made its Wall Street debut on Thursday (local time), with its valuation briefly touching $2 trillion and shares closing nearly 17% higher.Priced at $83 per share, the initial public offering ( IPO ) has also turned thousands of employees into millionaires on paper, including around 600 whose stock holdings are valued at more than $100 million.The windfall extends to early investors as well. Sound Ventures, founded by actor Ashton Kutcher and entertainment executive Guy Oseary, has valued its stake at $7.5 billion, while investment firm ICONIQ Capital's holding is estimated at $30 billion, Reuters reported.However, these are estimated paper fortunes. The actual wealth that founders, employees and investors can realise remains subject to lock-up periods, vesting conditions and changes in Anthropic's share price.The company's seven co-founders have individual stakes valued between $19.76 billion and $20.07 billion, based on the IPO price.The company's senior management also has substantial holdings. Krishna Rao, Anthropic's chief financial officer, has an estimated stake worth $788.3 million, according to Reuters.Anthropic's IPO has created a remarkable wealth pool among its employees. Around 5,100 staff members, representing 96% of its workforce, now have equity holdings worth more than $1 million.The figures are based on data from Hill.com, which tracks shares in privately held companies. According to regulatory filings, Anthropic had 5,300 employees as of September this year.Around 2,800 employees, known internally as “Ants”, hold shares valued at more than $10 million. Another 600 have crossed the $100 million mark, making them centi-millionaires.Andrew Benson, founder and CEO of Hill, told CNN on Thursday that the speed of wealth creation was particularly striking, especially given how few employees had left the company.“What’s most surprising here is how quickly this this happened,” Benson said.He added, “It’s been pretty clear for some time that Anthropic is a rocket ship, and so it definitely discouraged people from leaving because they knew what the opportunity cost of that would be.”The estimated values of the employees' stakes have been calculated based on a company filing. The figures for the founders, executives and employees are based on estimated holdings at the IPO price.Founded in 2021, Anthropic expanded rapidly from a small artificial intelligence startup to a company employing thousands of people. It had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024, but its workforce had grown to 5,300 by September this year.
Article Summary: Anthropic's IPO has created a remarkable wealth pool among its employees. Around 5,100 staff members, representing 96% of its workforce, now have equity holdings worth more than $1 million. The company's seven co-founders have individual stakes valued between $19.76 billion and $20.07 billion, based on the IPO price.

Article Title: Old Monk maker Mohan Meakin, India’s largest rum maker, faces revenue setback after FSSAI questions the composition and labelling of three rum variants produced at its Maharashtra facility; revenue dr
Article Text:
FSSAI also raised objections to product descriptions such as ‘7 Years Old Blended’ and ‘Very Old Vatted’. (Image source: Mohan Meakin wesbite)

FSSAI sales restrictions on some Old Monk variants

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s largest rum maker by volume, Mohan Meakin, which is known for its Old Monk has taken a serious revenue hit. The company saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year after food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility.The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.The unlisted company’s revenue from operations dropped 64% to Rs 288 crore during April-September, compared with Rs 792 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier, according to its latest financial results. The contraction was even steeper in the September quarter, with revenue falling 77% year-on-year to Rs 108 crore from Rs 473 crore.The sales restrictions were imposed after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) inspected the company’s manufacturing facility in Khopoli, according to an ET report..The regulator objected to the use of neutral spirit blended with rum flavouring, contending that such products could not be marketed as conventional rum and should instead be classified as rum-flavoured spirits.It also raised objections to product descriptions such as ‘7 Years Old Blended’ and ‘Very Old Vatted’.The facility has remained shut since May, according to the financial daily.Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries, the company that is responsible for manufacturing and bottling Old Monk in Maharashtra, challenged the FSSAI order before the Bombay High Court.However, it withdrew its petition on November 5, informing the court that it would submit revised labels directly to the regulator for approval. The court disposed of the petition as not pressed, leaving the sales restrictions in place.Mohan Meakin had earlier agreed to drop the claim that the rum had been aged for seven years and make information about the addition of flavouring more prominent on its labels. The regulator, however, maintained that the central dispute concerned how the product itself should be classified.At an October hearing, the company’s lawyers told the court that the restrictions had resulted in losses of around Rs 50 crore for the company and deprived the Maharashtra government of nearly Rs 350 crore in excise revenue. They also said that about 300 workers had been left without work.The regulatory setback comes at a time when Mohan Meakin has been working to restore Old Monk’s market position following years of declining sales, as whisky has gained dominance in India’s liquor market.The brand, which is around seven decades old and has long been associated with winter drinking, hostel rooftops and military canteens, saw its annual sales volume decline to 4.1 million cases in 2013 from a peak of 8 million cases in 2002.Sales subsequently recovered, and two years ago, Old Monk overtook United Spirits’ McDowell’s No. 1 Celebration to become India’s largest-selling rum brand by volume. The brand sold 14 million cases in 2025.The turnaround followed a leadership change after Brigadier Kapil Mohan, the company’s long-serving chairman, died in 2018.
Article Summary: Mohan Meakin saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year. Food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility. The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.

Article Title: Air India aims for greater synergy with Air India Express to cut costs
Article Text:
Greater synergy and integration between Air India and AI Express have emerged as a major way to cut costs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Greater synergy and integration between Air India and AI Express have emerged as a major way to cut costs, amid spiralling losses. At an Air India board meet here Friday chaired by N Chandrasekaran, the focus was on reducing losses as the AI group has lost over Rs 50,000 crore in just under five years after returning to the Tata fold and the promised capital-intensive revival is a bit distant in the future. Integration of roles at the full service and budget airlines to cut costs, rationalisation of loss-making routes and optimising revenue and fuel efficiency were the key focus areas at the meet. Some important decisions are likely to be conveyed to employees at a town hall that could be convened soon, say sources.Air India's loss widened to more than Rs 22,000 crore in FY26 due to multiple factors like fuel price rise, rupee depreciation and airspace closure restrictions that make western routes longer. AI's USP is being the only Indian carrier as of now that provides direct connectivity to faraway North America, Europe, Far East and Australia. With western routes affected, this USP can't be capitalised to the hilt.The board discussed operational and financial matters, to ensure operations are more cost-effective. A significant focus was on increasing fuel efficiency. Air India's new chief executive and MD Tewolde Gebremariam had earlier this month shared his plans for the airline's revival that sees more wide-body aircraft and a battle on costs.He feels AI has "punched below its weight" for too long and should "regain market share from competition (foreign airlines)" as that "business belongs to AI. "While the "short term" poses multiple "challenges", the "long term is a huge opportunity" and the deep-in-the-red airline could be profitable "very soon" by focusing on cutting costs and boosting revenue and efficiency.For this plan, Tewolde sought the board's approval on Friday, a day after the Tata top brass led by Noel Tata and Chandrasekaran visited the airline and aviation academy in Gurgaon.
Article Summary: Air India's loss widened to more than Rs 22,000 crore in FY26 due to multiple factors like fuel price rise, rupee depreciation and airspace closure restrictions that make western routes longer. Air India's new chief executive and MD Tewolde Gebremariam had earlier this month shared his plans for the airline's revival.

Article Title: Power & cement fuel October core sector growth of 10.9%
Article Text:
The growth marked acceleration from an upwardly revised figure of 8.2% in Sept.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The core sector grew 10.9% in Oct, driven by strong performance in the electricity, cement, iron ore and coal industries along with a favourable base effect, official data released Friday showed. Sequentially, the growth marked acceleration from an upwardly revised figure of 8.2% in Sept. This is the strongest performance of the core sector in the new series with the revised base year.During April-Oct, the core sector has grown 6% as compared to 2.3% a year ago. Output in the energy-dominant industries like natural gas (-7.6%), crude oil (-4.1%) and fertilisers (-12.2%) saw continued sequential contraction in Oct, reflecting the impact of the prolonged conflict in West Asia.Output in the refinery products (3.4%), though positive, saw sequential deceleration during the month.Output in the infrastructure-dominant industries such as electricity (21.6%), cement (15.4%), iron ore (26.4%) and steel (7.3%) showed sequential acceleration in Oct, reflecting the divergence in the growth trajectory of energy dominant and infrastructure dominant industries in recent months due to volatile crude prices.The core sector accounts for 40% weight in the index of industrial production (IIP) and is considered as a precursor of the performance of the country's wider industrial sector.
Article Summary: The growth marked acceleration from an upwardly revised figure of 8.2% in Sept. During April-Oct, the core sector has grown 6% as compared to 2.3% a year ago. The core sector accounts for 40% weight in the index of industrial production (IIP)

Article Title: Gold falls 4.49% to Rs 1.21 lakh, silver plunges 6.6% in a single day to Rs 1.47 lakh; wedding shoppers get a buying opportunity, with some families advancing jewellery purchases while others wait for
Article Text:
For households that had postponed jewellery purchases because of elevated prices, the correction offers an opportunity to reassess their budgets. (Image for representative purpose only)

Gold Price Crash Brings Cheer To Wedding Households

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gold and silver prices saw a steep decline on Friday, falling by as much as 6.6% as a firm US dollar, high bond yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy by the US Federal Reserve dampened investor sentiment.On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures dropped as much as 4.49%, or Rs 5,733, to Rs 1,21,719 per 10 grams from the previous close of Rs 1,27,452 per 10 grams. Silver futures faced even heavier selling, declining 6.6%, or Rs 10,416, to Rs 1,47,066 per kg.The sharp correction in the two precious metals also affected gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Nippon India ETF Gold BeES, ICICI Prudential Gold ETF and Quantum Gold ETF were among the funds that lost up to 5%, touching their respective 52-week lows during the session. Silver ETFs also came under significant pressure. Nippon India Silver ETF, ICICI Prudential Silver ETF and Mirae Asset Silver ETF were among those that declined by as much as 6%, hitting fresh 52-week lows.But, for households that had postponed jewellery purchases because of elevated prices, the correction offers an opportunity to reassess their budgets and bring forward planned purchases!Cheaper gold can substantially reduce the overall cost of jewellery, particularly for buyers planning to purchase heavier bridal sets, necklaces and bangles.While some consumers are waiting to see whether prices decline further, others have begun placing orders to take advantage of the lower rates.At EKARAA Jewellery, the fall in precious metal prices has prompted different reactions among customers. Mehul Jain, the company's founder, told ET that the savings were less significant for smaller ornaments but became more substantial for expensive, heavier pieces.“While smaller jewellery pieces have not seen a significant impact on overall budgets, the difference is more noticeable in heavier, high-value pieces, where even a slight change in metal prices can translate into considerable savings,” he was quoted as saying.Jain said some buyers were holding off on purchases in the hope of a further decline in prices. Others, however, were using the opportunity to select designs, discuss customisation requirements and plan wedding-related orders. The response indicates that changing gold prices are affecting not only the timing of jewellery purchases but also the way customers plan them.Zen Diamond India has also seen the benefit of softer gold prices, which have added momentum to an already strong sales trend. “Lower gold prices are certainly an incentive for consumers to advance their purchases, particularly with the wedding season approaching,” said Neil Sonawala, managing director of Zen Diamond India. “We expect this to translate into stronger demand in the coming weeks, especially among customers who have already planned their jewellery purchases. ”Yash Kataria, CEO of Kataria Jewellers, said the price decline had offered welcome relief to families preparing for weddings in the coming months. Even a modest reduction can make a difference when households need to purchase multiple jewellery pieces for the bride and other family members.According to Kataria, customers who had delayed buying in anticipation of lower prices were now reconsidering their plans. He suggested that families with weddings approaching should make purchases based on their actual requirements and budgets instead of waiting indefinitely for another price correction.Meanwhile, minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, released on Wednesday, indicated that nearly all policymakers believed interest rates would need to rise further to bring inflation under control.The prospect of tighter monetary policy has pushed bond yields higher and strengthened the US dollar, reducing the appeal of gold and silver to investors. Forced selling across financial markets has added to the downward pressure on the two metals.
Article Summary: Gold and silver prices saw a steep decline on Friday, falling by as much as 6.6% as a firm US dollar, high bond yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy by the US Federal Reserve dampened investor sentiment. For households that had postponed jewellery purchases because of elevated prices, the correction offers an opportunity to reassess their budgets.

Article Title: India, Canada push for wider market access as 6th round of trade talks ends
Article Text:
India, Canada wrap up Sixth round of CEPA talks, push for balanced trade pact

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India and Canada have wrapped up the sixth round of negotiations for their proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), with both sides pushing for an ambitious and balanced trade pact to expand market access, boost investments and strengthen economic ties. The talks, held in New Delhi from November 11 to 20, concluded on Friday, with progress reported across key areas of trade and investment.According to a release issued by the ministry of commerce and industry, the latest round covered several areas, including trade in goods and services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion.Towards the conclusion of the negotiations, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal met Canada's vice minister of International Trade Glenn Purves and his delegation in New Delhi. They reviewed the progress made during the sixth round and assessed the overall status of the CEPA discussions.Both sides reiterated their commitment to concluding an agreement that is ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful. They also stressed the need to ensure tangible benefits for farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries.The proposed pact is expected to open up additional opportunities for trade and investment.It also aims to strengthen resilient and diversified supply chains between the two countries.The sixth round began with a meeting between Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal and Canada's minister of international trade Maninder Sidhu in New Delhi on November 11.Both ministers emphasised the need for a balanced and mutually beneficial agreement. They said it should provide meaningful market access, build on the complementary strengths of the two economies and create fresh opportunities for trade and investment.The ministers also reviewed the progress of negotiations and guided their respective teams to advance discussions constructively, the ministry said.The Indian negotiating team was led by chief negotiator Brij Mohan Mishra, while the Canadian side was headed by chief negotiator Mary-Catherine Speirs.The ministry said substantive discussions took place across various negotiating tracks during the latest round, with both sides making progress towards advancing the proposed agreement.The negotiations are guided by the shared objective of concluding the pact within the ambitious timelines envisaged by the leaders of both countries, the release added.The conclusion of the sixth round reflects the continued engagement and commitment of India and Canada to take the negotiations forward and strengthen their bilateral economic and commercial relationship, the ministry said.
Article Summary: The talks, held in New Delhi from November 11 to 20, concluded on Friday. Both sides reiterated their commitment to concluding an agreement that is ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful. They stressed the need to ensure tangible benefits for farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Article Title: Lower tariff: Scotch companies caught in category flipping
Article Text:
The problem has its origins in product classification

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Scotch lobby may be making noise over tariffs not coming down for bulk whisky despite the India-UK trade agreement, but it is slowly emerging that the Scotch makers industry not only knew about the classification problems but also had got into litigation over the product code used to import at lower duties, which has now come back to haunt them.While govt officials maintain that India will honour its commitment and they are engaged to find a solution. The problem has its origins in product classification. As part of the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, govt has offered to allow bulk whisky classified as 220830 (six-digit product classification) at 75% tariff, while 220890, which stands for other unadulterated ethyl alcohol, attracts 110% duty. Unlike what the Scotch makers are claiming, no duty concession has been offered to products falling under classification 2106.Over three decades ago, Bussa Overseas and subsequently Pernod Ricard in 2008 challenged the classification. While Bussa argued that the product should be classified under tariff heading 220810 as it involved the import of bulk concentrates with 60-61% alcoholic strength, given the tariff advantage (this entry was later moved to 210690).Customs wanted it classified as finished potable spirits under heading 220830 but lost the case.With the trade deal in place, and 2106 outside the scope of concessions, the Scotch industry is seeking to flip the product classification from heading 2106 to 220890 - something that they woke up to after negotiators from both sides had finalised the agreement."A key concern for our industry is ensuring the inclusion of all our product's relevant tariff codes within the tariff liberalisation schedule. This includes those utilised for the export of bulk whisky products... Tariff code 22089099, which is currently used for the majority of bulk Scotch Whisky exports for regulatory reasons, was not liberalised to the same extent as the Scotch Whisky specific tariff codes, despite industry raising the importance of this," Scotch Whisky Association said in its submission to a parliamentary panel in the UK in Aug 2025."As things currently stand, this potentially means a significant proportion of Scotch Whisky exports will not benefit from the agreed tariff liberalisation, undermining the opportunities of this deal for the industry, as well as for the Indian industry which utilises bulk Scotch Whisky, either for bottling in country or as an ingredient in other products. The SWA underscored the importance of these specific inclusions throughout the negotiation process.This highlights the need for close, consistent, and meaningful business engagement throughout all stages of negotiations, including access to draft text, in order to avoid such situations from arising," it added.When caught seeking to reclassify bulk Scotch from 2106 to 220830 to take the tariff advantage, companies and industry bodies representing them sought to blame Indian customs authorities.
Article Summary: The problem has its origins in product classification. As part of the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, govt has offered to allow bulk whisky classified as 220830 (six-digit product classification) at 75% tariff. Unlike what the Scotch makers are claiming, no duty concession has been offered to products falling under classification 2106.

Article Title: Red carpet for FPIs': Congress slams Sebi plan to ease disclosure norms for foreign investors
Article Text:
Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh (Photo: ANI).

NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday criticised the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (Sebi) proposal to review additional disclosure requirements for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), saying credibility, transparency and investor protection were essential to efficient financial markets.The opposition party said the proposed changes were a step in the opposite direction and should be "buried", PTI reported.Sebi has proposed removing the additional disclosure framework that requires certain FPIs to provide granular details of entities holding ownership, economic interest or control in them. The regulator said the existing requirements go beyond beneficial ownership identification norms under anti-money laundering rules, making India's disclosure regime more stringent than those in several major global markets.Congress general secretary in-charge communications, Jairam Ramesh, said the consultation paper was issued soon after Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed industry leaders at FICCI on November 19, proposing to scrap disclosure rules introduced in August 2023 to identify opaque offshore investments in Indian companies."It is clear that the Prime Minister has little hope of reviving domestic private investment, or even FDI, and has decided instead to roll out the red carpet for foreign portfolio investors to keep the stock markets buoyant, even at the cost of market integrity," Ramesh said on X.India needed foreign investors, but not those with opaque and convoluted offshore ownership structures, he said, adding that ease of doing business could not come at the cost of capital market integrity.In August 2023, Sebi required FPIs with more than 50 per cent of their Indian equity investments in a single corporate group to provide detailed disclosures on ultimate ownership, economic interest and control, he said.The disclosures were intended to identify opaque ownership structures that could conceal concentrated control and create opportunities for market abuse, Ramesh added."Now, Sebi proposes to junk these requirements entirely. The loophole that was belatedly closed under pressure after the January 2023 revelations is being reopened," he said.Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey had earlier said the regulator would issue a consultation paper proposing further simplification of FPI regulations, including the removal of certain restrictions that are not present in other countries.Ramesh reiterated that transparency and investor protection were essential to maintaining the credibility of India's financial markets and said the proposed changes should be withdrawn.

Article Title: Empty Vande Bharat Express travels 463 kilometres with faulty brakes after railway staff ignore loco pilots’ warnings; South Eastern Railway orders probe into safety lapses
Article Text:
The SER zone subsequently issued an official order asking the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Ranchi to investigate the matter. (File photo of Vande Bharat)

Vande Bharat with faulty brakes runs empty

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

An empty Vande Bharat train travelled 463 km from Jharkhand to Uttar Pradesh in October despite concerns that its braking system was not functioning effectively. The incident has prompted the South Eastern Railway (SER) zone to order an investigation, as the movement of a train with inadequate braking posed a possible safety risk to other passenger services.The incident occurred on October 24, just days before the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed in Assam on November 11 in circumstances involving allegedly similar negligence, according to a PTI report.The rake, comprising empty Vande Bharat chair cars, was scheduled to be hauled by a goods locomotive from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh.According to railway officials, the braking arrangement of the passenger train had to be connected to the braking system of the freight locomotive assigned to pull it for the entire journey. However, railway personnel allegedly failed to ensure that the two systems were properly integrated. They also reportedly proceeded with the movement despite the train crew raising concerns about the braking performance.Highlighting the seriousness of the lapse, the railway zone said, "Running a train without adequate brake power is a serious safety concern that may lead to a major accident, endangering the lives of staff and passengers and affecting the safety of railway operations,"The SER zone subsequently issued an official order asking the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Ranchi to investigate the matter.The order stated that instructions had been issued on October 24 for the empty Vande Bharat rake to be transferred from Hatia to Jhansi.The document, dated November 7, recorded that the locomotive pilot had carried out the prescribed brake feel and brake power test after the train departed from Hatia. The check was conducted on the Hatia-Ranchi section, in keeping with the instructions then in force.The order stated, "As per the statement of the loco pilot, the brake feel and brake power test was conducted after departure from HTE (Hatia) in the HTE-RNC (Hatia-Ranchi) section, in accordance with the existing instructions in force,"However, the test reportedly revealed a serious problem with the train's ability to brake effectively. The order added, "However, during the test, the LP found that the brake power of the train was very poor and ineffective."When the train reached Ranchi station, the locomotive pilot formally reported the problem in writing to railway personnel, including the section controller and traction loco controller. His complaint specifically raised concerns about the inadequate braking power.Despite the warning, the rake was allowed to continue towards its destination without the reported problem being resolved. The railway zone's order noted, "The train was permitted to proceed in the same condition despite the reported poor brake power,"The railway zone’s order recorded that the problem persisted even after another locomotive pilot took charge of the train at Muri station. He, too, alerted the relevant controllers about the ineffective brakes, specifically pointing out that releasing the BP pressure did not activate them.Despite warnings from the train crew along the route, the issue was not addressed until the rake reached Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) station in Uttar Pradesh’s Chandauli district. Railway personnel at DDU then examined the train and discovered that the braking systems across all its coaches had been isolated, leaving the coaches without functioning brakes.The preliminary investigation attributed the incident to lapses involving several categories of railway personnel. These included coach and wagon (C&W) maintenance staff, section controllers and traction controllers at the stations concerned, as well as the crew responsible for operating the rake between Hatia and DDU.The inquiry specifically questioned the failure of C&W personnel to carry out a physical inspection of the braking systems before the empty rake was cleared for departure. Checking the condition and functioning of the train’s equipment was part of their maintenance responsibilities, the order noted according to the PTI report.It further pointed out that railway staff did not respond appropriately even after being informed that the train’s braking power was inadequate. The order also identified a gap in the train crew’s familiarity with Vande Bharat’s braking arrangement. Because they were unfamiliar with the system, the crew did not physically verify whether the brakes in the individual coaches were engaging.Summing up the findings, the order stated, "From the above, it is evident that there were multiple failures on the part of various staff, resulting in the train being worked without effective train brakes,"The document said the rake covered approximately 463 km without its coaches’ braking systems being used. During the journey, the train relied exclusively on the locomotive’s brakes and regenerative braking.Calling for a detailed examination of the incident, the railway zone concluded, "In view of the above, it is requested that the matter should be investigated in detail to ascertain the lapses on the part of the staff concerned. Necessary corrective and preventive measures may also be taken to prevent the recurrence of such incidents in the future,"
Article Summary: An empty Vande Bharat train travelled 463 km from Jharkhand to Uttar Pradesh in October despite concerns that its braking system was not functioning effectively. The incident occurred on October 24, just days before the Kolkata- Sairang Express derailed in Assam in circumstances involving allegedly similar negligence. The South Eastern Railway (SER) zone has ordered an investigation.

Article Title: Govt plans heavy penalty for number plate tampering to evade toll, fines of up to 8 times the fee

The penalty will be over and above the Motor Vehicles Act provision

NEW DELHI: Tampering with a vehicle number plate or hiding some part of it to evade toll payment at barrierless toll plazas is going to cost the vehicle owner dear, with govt set to impose penalties four to eight times the normal toll fee once such a vehicle is identified and caught.The penalty will be over and above the Motor Vehicles Act provision which prescribes a fine of Rs 5,000 for the first offence of tampering with a registration plate and Rs 10,000 for every subsequent violation. State transport departments can collect the penalty for the violation while highways authority like NHAI would be empowered to collect the higher toll charge.Road transport ministry is preparing a proposal to change the NH Fee Rules, provisioning for higher toll charges for such violations. Officials said a mechanism using photographs and details captured at toll plazas and artificial intelligence (AI) would be put in place in next couple of months to identify vehicles with manipulated or concealed registration numbers.On May 18, TOI had first reported NHAI’s flagging the problem of vehicle owners tampering with number plates to evade toll payments under the new system. Barely days after barrierless tolling started at Mundka plaza in Delhi, NHAI had written to Delhi govt for sustained surveillance.When other toll plazas were also made barrierless, the highways authority took this up with other state govts.This is crucial for ensuring the success of barrierless tolling across the National Highway (NH) network, wherein vehicles can pass through without stopping and toll charges are collected electronically. “Until there is 100% compliance of vehicles having High Security Number Plates or readable registration numbers, the problem will persist. Though the problem pertains to barely 2-4% of vehicles, mostly smaller and local vehicles, the focus is on eliminating it,” said a person privy to govt plans.
Article Summary: Tampering with a vehicle number plate or hiding some part of it to evade toll payment at barrierless toll plazas is going to cost the vehicle owner dear. Road transport ministry is preparing a proposal to change the NH Fee Rules, provisioning for higher toll charges for such violations.

Article Title: Bharat Rice sales plunge after withdrawal of subsidy, reveals RTI reply
Article Text:
Bharat Rice was launched in February 2024

NEW DELHI: Sales of Bharat Rice have plunged sharply after the Centre withdrew the subsidy provided under the scheme, falling from around 14.6 lakh tonnes in its first phase in 2024 to just 82,088 tonnes in the third phase (July 2025-June 2026), an RTI reply has revealed.The subsidy, which was initially Rs 5.4 per kg, was reduced to Rs 2 per kg in the second phase before being completely withdrawn from July 2025. Govt has not provided any support from the Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF) since then.The information was disclosed by the food department in response to an RTI application filed by Kerala-based RTI activist K Govindan Nampoothiry.Launched on Feb 6, 2024, Bharat Rice was aimed at providing rice to consumers at subsidised rates under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic). Food Corporation of India (FCI) sells excess stocks from the central pool through three cooperative organisations: NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar.According to the reply, as against an allocation of 17.5 lakh tonnes in the first phase (Feb-June 2024), 14.6 lakh tonnes of rice were sold. Sales fell to 2.7 lakh tonnes in the second phase (July 2024-June 2025) compared with an allocation of 2.9 lakh tonnes. In the third phase (July 2025-June 2026), sales dropped further to 82,088 tonnes as against the 1.6 lakh tonnes allocated.The decline has continued in the ongoing fourth phase. As against an allocation of three lakh tonnes for July 2026-June 2027, only 5,886 tonnes have been sold, the reply dated Nov 13, 2026, said.Nampoothiry said the sharp fall in sales and withdrawal of subsidy raised questions about the govt’s efforts to make affordable rice available at a time of rising food prices. He called for urgent steps to contain the increase in rice prices.
Article Summary: Bharat Rice was launched on Feb 6, 2024, aimed at providing rice to consumers at subsidised rates. The subsidy, which was initially Rs 5.4 per kg, was reduced to Rs 2 per kg in the second phase before being completely withdrawn from July 2025.

However, when the Centralised Processing Centre (CPC), Bengaluru, processed her return, it determined a tax payable at Rs 75,502 without allowing the rebate.The assessee challenged the denial before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals). The first appellate authority rejected her explanation and upheld the denial. She then approached the Hyderabad bench of the ITAT.Her authorised representative argued that neither Section 87A nor Section 115BAC(1A) expressly barred the rebate merely because part of the taxpayer’s income was taxable under Section 111A.The representative also relied on two earlier tribunal decisions:, decided by the ITAT Ahmedabad bench, and, decided by the ITAT Mumbai bench. Article Text:
Sebi’s own research showed that granular disclosure requirements under ADF were unique to India.

MUMBAI: Hours after chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said that the markets regulator was in the process of coming out with a consultation paper on foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), Sebi published a paper saying it intends to do away with the stringent rule relating to the additional disclosure framework (ADF). This requires select FPIs to disclose granular details relating to who all have invested in their funds that are invested in India.A comparative analysis of various jurisdictions around the world showed that Sebi's rules were more stringent than others. In addition, Sebi also asks for an additional disclosure framework (ADF) under which select FPIs are "required to submit granular details of all entities holding any ownership, economic interest, or exercising control in the FPI, on a full look through basis, up to the level of all natural persons, without any threshold.Sebi's own research showed that granular disclosure requirements under ADF were unique to India. "Disclosure requirements that are not in line with globally accepted practices could potentially place India at a competitive disadvantage vis-a-vis peer jurisdictions with relatively lenient regulatory requirements," the paper said.

Article Title: Systematic withdrawal: EPFO seeks income tax tweaks
Article Text:
The remaining balance will continue to earn returns, providing members with a regular income stream after retirement while preserving their savings.

NEW DELHI: EPFO is seeking amendments in the Income Tax Act to ensure that monthly payouts under its newly approved systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) are legally recognised as staged withdrawals, and not as a pension, while also proposing to delink provident fund (PF) membership from traditional employer-employee relationship.The retirement body wants clarity that periodic installments drawn by retirees - whether drawn monthly, quarterly or annually - are treated solely as a systematic drawdown of their own accumulated savings balance rather than an annuity or pension payout. PF withdrawals at present are structured around final lump-sum settlements upon retirement."The matter has been conveyed to the ministry to pursue the matter with the finance ministry. The approval is expected to come soon, with SWP operationalisation kicking soon," a person familiar with the development told TOI. Under SWP, retiring members are being provided with the opportunity to withdraw only a part of their PF corpus and earn interest on the remaining amount. The facility will not be available to members of exempted PF trusts in the initial phase.In order to enable social security coverage for the vast unorganised workers, EPFO has also proposed breaking the link between PF participation and formal payroll employment.Under existing norms, active EPF membership and contributions are tied to an employer-employee relationship. EPFO wants the framework amended so that retired members, platform workers and unorganised sector labourers can continue as active members and contribute independently.The retirement fund body has also sought to remove the requirement that PF contributions must originate from "salary". Since gig workers, unorganised labourers and retirees do not earn conventional monthly wages, the amendment will allow them to deposit irregular earnings directly into their Universal Account Number (UAN), while enabling third-party micro-contributions such as incentives or customer tips.To make solo retirement saving viable where there is no matching employer share, EPFO has requested raising annual contribution limit for self or third-party deposits to Rs 5 lakh, bringing it on a par with the general provident fund threshold for govt employees.
Article Summary: EPFO is seeking amendments in the Income Tax Act to ensure that monthly payouts under its newly approved systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) are legally recognised as staged withdrawals. It is also proposing to delink provident fund (PF) membership from traditional employer-employee relationship.

Article Title: Noel asks for recordings of Tata Sons meet again
Article Text:
Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts

Noel Tata on Friday again sought video recordings of the Sept 3 Tata Sons nomination and remuneration (NRC) meeting and the Sept 17 Tata Sons board meeting that culminated in N Chandrasekaran 's reappointment as chairman. The company had earlier rejected his demand, saying it was not legally required to share or retain recordings of in-person meetings with directors.The Tata Trusts chairman, who is also a Tata Sons director, has now asked the company to "preserve" the recordings of both the NRC meeting and the board meeting.In a seven-page letter dated Nov 20 to company secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay, copied to all directors, he sought written responses by Nov 25, a day before the Tata Sons board meets.Noel argued that directors were entitled to inspect the company's electronic records and that Article 129 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association (AoA) did not exclude such access. He warned that any deletion or alteration after Sept 18, when he first sought preservation, would amount to "deliberate destruction of evidence" and offered to inspect the recordings at Bombay House, Tata Group’s headquarters, in the presence of an adviser.Noel again disputed the minutes of the Sept 17 board meeting and reiterated that no resolution on Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third term had been validly passed under Articles 118 and 121 of the AoA.While Tata Sons had listed a "debrief from the NRC" as an agenda item for the Sept 17 board meeting, Noel maintained that the agenda did not provide for a resolution on Chandrasekaran's reappointment, which was nevertheless taken up.He also contended that the NRC minutes circulated to him were only a draft and did not bear the signatures of committee members.The final minutes of the Sept 17 board meeting will come up for approval at the Tata Sons board’s Nov 26 meeting, where directors can either approve them or record their objections.Noel asked that the board consider his objections before finalising the minutes.He said the reappointment required the affirmative vote of a majority of the Trusts' directors present at the Sept 17 meeting. One of the two voted in favour and the other against. Noel disputed the use of the chairman's casting vote to break the tie, arguing that the provision did not authorise it.Noel also renewed his objection to Tata Sons' filing with the Registrar of Companies stating that Chandrasekaran was reappointed for another five years, a step he says was never validly taken.He renewed his conflict-of-interest objection over the business relationship between TVS Motor Co, associated with Venu Srinivasan, and Hanno One Warehousing, a company linked to members of Chandrasekaran's family.Noel contended that Srinivasan, a Tata Trusts trustee and Tata Sons director, should have recused himself from the NRC proceedings that recommended Chandrasekaran for a third term. Srinivasan also voted for the reappointment at the Sept 17 board meeting.Tata Sons previously rejected the conflict-of-interest argument, saying Hanno One has no transactions with Tata Sons or any Tata group entity. It maintained that a contract awarded by TVS Motor to a company in which Chandrasekaran's family has a disclosed interest does not create a conflict with Tata Sons. Noel said that response missed the point. The issue, he said, was whether directors involved in evaluating the executive chairman and considering his reappointment could exercise independent judgement.Noel also questioned Tata Sons' Oct 6 letter to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in which the company said it intended to comply with the regulator's norms and was keen to take steps towards doing so. He said the letter had neither been shown to him nor placed before the board before it was sent. He disputed the company's interpretation that the Sept 17 board meeting had authorised it to pursue a listing, saying directors had agreed only to explore alternatives and seek guidance from RBI.RBI replied on Nov 16, telling Tata Sons to comply with its rules, including the requirement to list.He also asked that the Trusts' Sept 28 merger proposal, which he said would let Tata Sons cease to be classified as a non-banking financial company without a listing, be circulated to directors ahead of the Nov 26 meeting, along with management's assessment of it and the legal advice received.He asked Tata Sons to send RBI nothing beyond an acknowledgement, take no steps towards a listing and make no changes to its AoA or capital structure until the board decided how to proceed.
Article Summary: Noel Tata has asked the company to "preserve" the recordings of both the NRC meeting and the board meeting. The company had earlier rejected his demand, saying it was not legally required to share or retain recordings of in-person meetings with directors.

MUMBAI: Record foreign buying pushed the sensex up 898 points, or 1.1%, on Friday to 83,920, its highest close in nine months, taking foreign portfolio inflows in Nov past Rs 1.3 lakh crore, an all-time high for monthly flows. FPIs net bought stocks worth Rs 10,308 crore on Friday, BSE data showed, adding to the Rs 1.2 lakh crore invested till Thursday, according to NSDL data.The buying lifted the rupee to 92.67 against the dollar, nearly 4.5% above its record low of 96.96 in May. The currency gained around 1.75% this week from 94.3.Sensex has gained over 9,300 points, or nearly 13%, this month even as global AI-linked stocks came under pressure. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has fallen over 6% and South Korea's Kospi has declined around 15%. Nifty rose 286 points to close at 25,801. Friday's rally added around Rs 2.2 lakh crore to investor wealth, taking the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies to Rs 514.2 lakh crore, or around $5.5 trillion. Private banks led the gains, with the BSE Bankex and NSE Bank Nifty scaling record highs.According to market participants, strong foreign inflows and a shift away from global AI-linked investments supported the rupee. "The rupee witnessed a strong rally, gaining around 0.75% to 92.66... Strong foreign fund flows continue to provide support to the domestic currency," said a market expert, who expects the currency to trade between 92.25 and 93 in the near term.Foreign exchange reserves, however, fell by more than $14 billion week-on-week to $705.3 billion in the week ended Nov 13, their lowest level in about three months, RBI data released on Friday showed. Foreign currency assets declined by $7.8 billion and gold holdings by $6.1 billion.According to Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments, foreign investors shifting away from global AI trades supported private banks, while easing concerns over AI disruption helped Indian IT stocks. "Private banks extended their record run as foreign investors... continued to favour the sector's liquidity which are trading at reasonable valuation," he said.

FPIs net bought stocks worth Rs 10,308 crore on Friday, adding to the Rs 1.2 lakh crore invested till Thursday. The buying lifted the rupee to 92.67 against the dollar.
